meaning: at the moment of / on the momentum of doing X, (unintentionally) Y happened

exercises.example_sentence: 転んだ弾みに、手をついて手首をひねってしまった。
exercises.translation: When I fell, I put out my hand and ended up spraining my wrist.
wrong_choice_explanations: ついでに means 'while at it', using an occasion to do something deliberately. 転んだついでに手首をひねった would make spraining the wrist intentional; 弾みに gives the accidental result of the fall.
あげく means 'after a long process, in the end (badly)'. 転んだあげく needs a drawn-out struggle, but the fall and sprain happened in an instant; 弾みに gives the momentum of the fall.
きり means 'did and then stayed that way'. 転んだきり would mean the speaker fell and never got up, which doesn't connect to putting out a hand; 弾みに gives the injury caused by the fall.

きり means 'did and then stayed that way'. 閉めたきり would mean the door stayed shut afterwards, unrelated to the vase falling; 弾みに links the slam to the vase breaking.
あげく means 'after a long process, in the end (badly)'. 閉めたあげく needs a drawn-out struggle, but slamming a door is a single motion; 弾みに gives its instant knock-on effect.
